required_units: The retained delivered-plan record changed from an initially direct route to later non-direct routes while the requested goal remained fixed.
All 74 delivered plans had unique hashes; the first plan had 0.000 m maximum lateral deviation and later plans spanned -1.407 m to +1.231 m signed lateral deviation.
Delivered odometry reached 1.301 m maximum lateral deviation and NavigateToPose succeeded after 77.760 s.
The retained rolling costmap covers only part of the requested route, so it cannot establish the physical trigger for the plan changes.
Delivered plans do not prove controller consumption, and the record does not establish observation-to-plan causation or a specific obstacle identity.
The answer recommends time-aligning planner inputs, emitted paths, controller path updates, and costmap observations before attributing a trigger.
prohibited_claims: A particular obstacle or physical condition caused the delivered plan changes.
The controller consumed every delivered plan.
A delivered costmap observation caused a particular plan change.
The retained rolling grid proves global route infeasibility or complete route clearance.
Zero recovery feedback proves that exactly zero recoveries occurred over a complete goal history.
The successful action has a terminal failure chain.

limits: Delivered plans are not proof of controller consumption.
Delivered odometry is not proof of Nav2 internal consumed state.
Temporal ordering does not establish observation-to-plan causation.
The final rolling costmap does not cover the complete requested route.
Evaluator layout and obstacle identity are unavailable to methods and the judge.
The case is development-only, not held-out or confirmatory evidence.
